title: Integrality from a pairwise intersecting affine domain cover
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a nonempty set, and let $(V_i)_{i\in I}$ be an affine open covering of $Y$, with specified isomorphisms $V_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for commutative rings $A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose that every $A_i$ is an integral domain (a nonzero ring in which $xy=0$ implies $x=0$ or $y=0$), and that $V_i\cap V_j\ne\varnothing$ for all $i,j\in I$. Then $Y$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. No separatedness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 01OL (lemma-characterize-reduced), 01OM (lemma-characterize-irreducible), and 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral): combined affine-cover criterion, using their displayed statements and proofs, lines 197–276.

proof.text: For each $i$, the domain hypothesis and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field](2) make $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ integral. The specified scheme isomorphism identifies this scheme with $V_i$, so $V_i$ is integral. By the explicit equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme], every $V_i$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible.

Apply [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-open-cover] to the given open cover and the reducedness of its members from Step 1. Thus $Y$ is reduced. Choose $i_0\in I$; the nonempty subset $V_{i_0}\subseteq Y$ also shows that $Y$ is nonempty.

We verify irreducibility using [def-weil-irreducible-components], following Tag 01OM. Suppose $Y=Z_1\cup Z_2$ with $Z_1,Z_2$ closed. Irreducibility of $V_{i_0}$ implies that $V_{i_0}\subseteq Z_1$ or $V_{i_0}\subseteq Z_2$; interchange the labels so the former holds. For each $j$, $O=V_{i_0}\cap V_j$ is a nonempty open subset of $V_j$ contained in $Z_1$. If $V_j\not\subseteq Z_1$, then $P=V_j\setminus Z_1$ is another nonempty open subset of $V_j$, disjoint from $O$. Their closed complements $V_j\setminus O$ and $V_j\setminus P$ would cover $V_j$, with neither equal to $V_j$, contradicting its irreducibility. Hence every $V_j\subseteq Z_1$. Since these opens cover $Y$, $Y=Z_1$. Together with nonemptiness, this proves irreducibility. Intersections here are only open subsets; they are never assumed affine.
Steps 2 and 3 give nonemptiness, reducedness and irreducibility. The equivalence stated in [def-pc-integral-scheme] (Tag 01ON) therefore implies that $Y$ is integral.
